items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: One of the people who used to come up that I remember is a guy named Marty Emerson, who was a trombone player...

ctx.x: sideways, and he'd look up at me and say, 'Hi, John, how you doin'?' -- his left hand is going a mile a minute. 'Did you work tonight? Did you see so-and-so-and-so today?' or something. And I'd exchange some quick hello's with him. And he'd have his drink, and he'd probably sit there playing a couple of choruses with just his left hand. Then he'd go back into it, then finally finish that hour. I don't know who was keeping time for him, but afterwards everybody would be shaking their head in amazement.

One of the people who used to come up that I remember is a guy named Marty Emerson, who was a trombone player, him and a guy named Jack Schaeffer, who was a trumpet player. I think Jack Schaeffer went to Las Vegas. I don't know if he's still around or not. But Marty Emerson is now Secretary of the international body of the American Federation of Musicians. If you ever get the International newspaper or have anything to do with the American Federation of Musicians, Marty Emerson is the Secretary, and he's a big…

Anyway, those were just some memorable days in shaping, you know, every approach that I had to music. And these associations... You aren't aware of it when they're happening, but they have an indelible stamp on you for life. The big bands and the little band that I had...
